mirrored_block.description:
The mirror commits inside each block's unit of work, so it is
current to this height: `evaluated_block`.

action.description:
`trip_function`, `trip_global`, `reset_function`,
`reset_global` or `call`. Reset kinds exist only here: rules
never unpause anything. `call` invokes a declared function on
the target directly and needs no controller: the manual route
for contracts guarded by their own `pause()`.

args.description: The call's literal arguments, one string each, for `call`.

function.description: The called signature form, for `call`, e.g. `pause()`.

selector.description: The 4-byte selector, for the controller function-level kinds.

enabled.description:
Whether the rule starts enabled; an agent-submitted rule
starting disabled is the caller's policy, expressed here.

origin.description: Who wrote it: `app`, `mcp` or `api`; recorded for attribution.

age_seconds.description: Seconds since the cursor last moved.

DependencyOut.description: One unwatched dependency of a rule.

first_block.description: The block whose evaluation first touched it.

document.description:
The document in canonical form. Series keys are assigned by
the engine, derived canonically from each call; callers never
invent them.

ErrorBody.description: The plain error envelope on every other non-2xx answer.

ErrorInfo.description: The error envelope every non-2xx answer carries.

message.description: What happened, why, and what to do about it.

error.description:
Set when the rule cannot be judged: the failing node's
JSON-pointer path and what happened.

evidence.description:
The evidence tree, every node's value exactly as a violation
would carry it.

warming.description:
Some metric is still warming: "cannot yet know", as opposed
to "would not trip". `needs.warmup_seconds` says how long.

would_trip.description:
`trip_when` holds now. The polarity is the language's:
`trip_when` states the violation, so true means the bad
condition holds; a caller whose users write conditions that
must hold translates at its own boundary.

cause.description: What degrades the engine, when something does.

oneOf.description:
The mirrored controller; absent when none is configured
or the engine is still starting.

evaluated_block.description: The last block the evaluator committed.

oneOf.description: The signer summary; absent while starting.
The mempool summary; absent when disabled or starting.

observed_head.description: The head the follower last observed on the node.

InvalidDocument.description:
The `400` shape of an invalid rule document: the envelope plus
every issue the validator found, all at once, exactly as the
validator reports them.

IssueOut.description: One validation failure, exactly as the validator reports it.

balance.description:
The key's native balance at the current block, wei as a
decimal string: whether it can pay for gas.

candidates_dropped.description: Candidates shed to keep the queue bound.

candidates_seen.description: Pending transactions the stream has delivered.

last_error.description: Why it does not, when it does not.

function.description:
The signature form with its return declaration, e.g.
`balanceOf(address) returns (uint256)`.

error.description: Why this call failed, when it did.

values.description:
The decoded return components: quantities as decimal strings,
tuples as arrays. Absent when the call failed.

gas_estimate.description: The node's (or the fork's) gas estimate, when it executes.

ok.description: The action would execute at the current head.

preview.description:
The decoded call, exactly as the approval queue would show
it: target, function, decoded_args, value.

revert_reason.description: Why it would not, when it would not.

dependencies.description:
The rule's unwatched dependencies (detection R57,
store-and-interface R58): every contract its evaluations
touched that it neither names nor watches, stored once with the
block that first touched it. Replacing the document clears
them; `api_v1.rules.dependencies` carries the same list.

needs.description:
What evaluating the rule requires (reads, events, series,
`warmup_seconds`).

trace.description:
On create and replace: every contract the rule's reads,
`verify` and simulations touch, at any depth, walking every
branch (store-and-interface R55). Absent when the trace did not
finish within 5 s or the chain could not be read; the rule is
stored regardless, and `POST /v1/rules/trace` answers the same.

trace_skipped.description:
With `trace`: the nodes the trace could not evaluate (a
reverting read, an `event_arg` with no log). Empty means every
branch was walked through.

SkippedOut.description:
A node a trace could not evaluate; reads beneath it that did run
are still in the trace.

complete.description:
True when every node was evaluated: every branch and every read
ran. False when some node was skipped (see `skipped`).

skipped.description:
The nodes the trace could not evaluate, each with its JSON
pointer and why: a reverting read (what it reached before
reverting is still listed), or an `event_arg`, which has no log
to read outside an event. Every other branch was still walked.

TracedOut.description: One contract in a rule's trace.

role.description:
`named` (the rule names it), `watched` (in its `watch`) or
`unwatched` (read through the rule but neither).

touched.description:
Whether this evaluation reached it; a named or watched
contract can be cold right now.

amount_wei.description:
Decimal wei, or the literal `"all"`: the balance minus a fee
reserve that keeps every escalation payable.

to.description: The recipient address. Destinations are not judged.

info.description: The localhost HTTP API through which every mutation and action flows, plus a server-sent event stream of what the engine sees. Reads of records come from the api_v1 views (see contract/views.json); this interface is how the application changes the engine. Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <interface secret>`; anything else is 401. Errors are `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }` with a fitting status; an invalid rule document is 400 with `issues`, every issue at once. Every on-chain quantity is a decimal string. Mutations return the resulting resource.
info.title: Tripwire engine control interface

post.summary:
A person pausing or unpausing from the dashboard during an
incident: the same pre-flight, signing, submission and receipt
watch as a response, recorded in `api_v1.actions` with its note.

Register a contract. The ABI is stored with it (it serves
decoding and authoring); reads of contracts come from the views.

409.description: One of its rules has a live response

delete.summary:
Remove a contract and, by the store's cascades, its rules and
their history; the compiled set reloads before the answer.

patch.summary: Update a contract's name and ABI. Absent fields keep their value.

get.summary:
The live stream. Named events (`block`, `violation`,
`rule_state`, `trip_state`, `response`, `notification`,
`health`), payloads mirroring the corresponding view rows.

The live process speaking for itself; liveness while the engine
is down is the views' job (`engine_status`).

200.description: Every key in the keys directory

get.summary:
The keys on disk with their lock status and native balance at the
current block.

post.summary:
Generate a key in-process and write its keystore file. The key
starts unlocked; its material never leaves the engine.

Import a keystore made elsewhere: it must decrypt with the given
passphrase; the imported key starts locked.
Drop the signer; the decrypted material zeroes on the way out.

Decrypt the key into a memory-locked signer. A wrong passphrase
is `400` and names nothing further.

Send ETH out of an operator key: recorded as a manual action of
kind `withdraw`, driven on the key's own transaction lane with
the usual pre-flight, receipt watch and escalation. The named
key signs, whether or not it is the configured response signer.

get.summary: Prometheus text: what the engine has done since it started.

200.description: One result per call, in order

post.summary:
Execute view calls at the current head on the local fork:
read-only, stores nothing, rejects state-changing functions on
execution evidence.

200.description: Whether the action would execute, with its preview

post.summary:
Build a rule's on-chain action exactly as a trip would and
simulate it at the current head: nothing is sent, nothing is
stored. A missing operator grant shows here, before an incident.

200.description: The response as it now stands (the api_v1.responses row)

post.summary:
Approve a held response: preconditions re-checked, rebuilt if the
chain moved under it, then submitted. `409` when the response is
not awaiting approval.
Reject a held response: `abandoned`, with the reason on file.

400.description: Invalid document; issues carry every failure

post.summary:
Create a rule: validate against the rule language, store canonically,
hot-reload, and return the canonical document, sentence and
needs. An invalid document is `400` with every issue at once.

200.description: The evaluation at the current head

400.description: Invalid document; issues carry every failure

post.summary:
A full check of a rule document with no side effects: the store
is byte-identical before and after. Metric nodes use recorded
history when their series already exists and report warming
otherwise.

The batch form: all rows in one transaction, so switching a
contract's worth of rules is all-or-nothing; one reload covers
the batch.

400.description: Invalid document; issues carry every failure

502.description: The chain could not be read (`chain_unreadable`)

503.description: The trace did not finish within 10 s, waiting for the one trace slot included (`trace_timeout`); nothing was stored, try again

post.summary:
Trace a rule document (store-and-interface R55): every contract
its reads, `verify` and simulations touch at the current head, at
any depth, each marked named, watched or unwatched. The walk takes
every `and`/`or` branch and continues past a read that fails, so
a dependency is listed whatever the current verdict. Nothing is
stored or sent; the owner picks what to `watch` from the result.
One trace runs at a time; a trace that has not finished within
10 s, waiting included, answers 503 `trace_timeout`.

409.description: The rule has a live response

delete.summary: Delete a rule and its history.

patch.summary:
Enable or disable one rule. A disabled rule leaves the compiled
set; its document, history and any queued responses stay.

put.summary:
Replace a rule's document; identity and history persist. Its
stored unwatched dependencies are cleared: they belonged to the old
document.

404.description: No such rule, or the rule has no unwatched dependency at that address

post.summary:
Acknowledge one of a rule's unwatched dependencies
(store-and-interface R58): the owner has seen it and chooses not to
watch it. Idempotent; answers the rule's whole list.
